title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 13
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Five advertising campaigns:

Alpha: GBP 4,800.00 spent, 12,000 visitors, 3% of them converted
Beta: GBP 9,200.00 spent, 40,000 visitors, 1.6% of them converted
Gamma: GBP 2,700.00 spent, 5,000 visitors, 4.5% of them converted
Delta: GBP 6,400.00 spent, 16,000 visitors, 2.5% of them converted
Epsilon: GBP 5,500.00 spent, 25,000 visitors, 1.1% of them converted

Which campaign bought conversions most cheaply?
questions.explanation: Conversions are visitors multiplied by the rate: Alpha 360, Beta 640, Gamma 225, Delta 400, Epsilon 275. Dividing spend by conversions: Alpha GBP 13.33, Beta GBP 14.38, Gamma GBP 12.00, Delta GBP 16.00, Epsilon GBP 20.00. Gamma is cheapest at GBP 12.00 a conversion, on the smallest budget in the table. Beta wins the most conversions outright but pays more for each one.

questions.prompt:
Annual output:

2019: 340
2020: 402
2021: 515
2022: 668
2023: 690
2024: 812

In which year did output first exceed double the 2019 figure?
questions.explanation: Double the 2019 figure is 680. 2022 reaches 668, still 12 short, and 2023 is the first year above it at 690. The largest single jump comes earlier, between 2021 and 2022, which is a different question.

questions.prompt:
Cumulative results for 400 candidates:

scored 40 or below: 36
scored 50 or below: 104
scored 60 or below: 218
scored 70 or below: 322
scored 80 or below: 379
scored 100 or below: 400

What proportion of candidates scored above 60?
questions.explanation: 218 candidates scored 60 or below, so 400 − 218 = 182 scored above it, which is 45.5%. 54.5% is the share at or below 60 — the complement, and the figure the table gives directly.

questions.prompt:
Two sets of five readings:

Set P: 48, 49, 50, 51, 52
Set Q: 30, 40, 50, 60, 70

Which statement about the two sets is accurate?
options: A. Set P has the higher mean
B. The two sets share a mean and a median, but Q is far more spread out
C. Set Q has the higher median
D. The two sets have the same range
E. Set P is more spread out than set Q
questions.explanation: Both sets have a mean of 50 and a middle value of 50, so the two averages say nothing to tell them apart. The ranges differ sharply: 4 for P against 40 for Q. Spread is the only one of these measures that separates them.

questions.prompt:
A budget of GBP 9,500.00 is to buy as many machines as possible at GBP 780.00 each.

Select the number bought AND the amount left over.
questions.explanation: GBP 9,500.00 divided by GBP 780.00 is 12.18, so 12 machines can be bought, costing GBP 9,360.00 and leaving GBP 140.00. A 13th machine would need GBP 640.00 more than the budget allows.

questions.prompt:
A van costing GBP 28,000.00 loses 18% of its value each year.

Select its value after 3 years AND the total value lost over those 3 years.
questions.explanation: Each year the van keeps 82% of its value, so after 3 years it is worth GBP 28,000.00 × 0.82³ = GBP 15,438.30, having lost GBP 12,561.70. Taking 18% of the original price away three times gives GBP 12,880.00, too low, because each year's loss is charged on a smaller value than the last.

questions.prompt:
Two firms in different markets:

Firm One: 34% of a market worth GBP 42 million
Firm Two: 61% of a market worth GBP 21 million

Select the firm with the larger market share AND the firm with the larger revenue.
options: A. Firm One on both measures
B. Firm Two on both measures
C. Firm Two on market share; Firm One on revenue
D. The two firms are equal on both measures
E. Firm One on market share; Firm Two on revenue
questions.explanation: Revenue is share multiplied by market size: Firm One GBP 14.28 million, Firm Two GBP 12.81 million. Firm Two holds much the larger share but of a market half the size, so Firm One takes more money. A share is only as valuable as the market it is a share of.

questions.prompt:
A courier charges GBP 6.50 for the first 5 kg and GBP 1.15 for each further kilogram.

Select the cost of a 23 kg parcel AND the lowest whole weight at which the cost first exceeds GBP 30.00.
questions.explanation: Only 23 − 5 = 18 kg is charged at the extra rate: GBP 6.50 + 18 × GBP 1.15 = GBP 27.20. At 25 kg the cost is GBP 29.50, still under GBP 30.00; at 26 kg it reaches GBP 30.65. Charging all 23 kg at the extra rate gives GBP 32.95.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): pupils on roll — School A 1,250, School B 480, School C 2,100

SOURCE 2 (table): pupils meeting the standard — School A 875, School B 360, School C 1,428

SOURCE 3 (memo): "The award goes to the school with the highest proportion of its pupils meeting the standard."

Which school receives the award?
options: C. The three schools are equal
D. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Proportions meeting the standard: School A 70.0%, School B 75.0%, School C 68.0%. School B is highest and is by some way the smallest school. School C gets 1,428 pupils over the line, more than any other, but has the most pupils to start with.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Sales reached GBP 4.2 million this year, against GBP 5 million last year — a fall of 16%."

SOURCE 2 (note): this year's figure covers 9 months; the accounting year was shortened.

SOURCE 3 (table): last year covered twelve months.

Which statement is best supported?
options: B. Sales were flat between the two years
C. The comparison cannot be made at all
D. Comparing 9 months against twelve understates this year, which is running ahead at the same monthly rate
E. Monthly sales fell between the two years
questions.explanation: GBP 4.2 million over 9 months is GBP 0.47 million a month, or GBP 5.6 million over twelve — above last year's GBP 5 million. The headline fall is an artefact of the shorter period. The comparison can be made once the periods are put on the same footing, so "cannot be made at all" goes too far.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): price per pallet — Haulier A GBP 14.20, Haulier B GBP 16.80, Haulier C GBP 15.40

SOURCE 2 (table): capacity a week — Haulier A 600 pallets, Haulier B 1,200 pallets, Haulier C 950 pallets

SOURCE 3 (email): "We must move 900 pallets in a single week, at the lowest total cost, using one haulier."

Which haulier should be used?
options: D. All three cost the same
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Haulier A is cheapest per pallet but can move only 600 in a week, short of the 900 required. Of the two with the capacity, Haulier B would charge GBP 15,120.00 and Haulier C would charge GBP 13,860.00, so Haulier C is the choice. Capacity settles who is eligible before price settles who wins.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Cost per unit fell from GBP 8.40 to GBP 7.10."

SOURCE 2 (table): the workforce grew from 210 to 260.

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board wants to know whether total production costs rose."

Which single further fact would settle the board's question?
options: A. The average wage of the staff taken on
B. The cost per unit at a competitor
C. The number of units produced in each year
D. The selling price of each unit
E. The size of the workforce five years ago
questions.explanation: Total cost is units multiplied by cost per unit. Source 1 gives the second factor for both years but nothing gives the first, so the total can move either way: at 400,000 units both years the total falls, while a large enough rise in output would push it up. Headcount is not a substitute, because the sources never link staff to units.

questions.prompt:
What is the perimeter of a triangle?

(1) Two of its sides measure 5 cm and 9 cm.
(2) The triangle is isosceles.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) leaves the third side open, and (2) alone gives no lengths at all. Together the third side must match one of the two given, so it is 5 or 9, and the perimeter is 19 cm or 23 cm. Both are genuine triangles, since 5, 5 and 9 obey the triangle inequality, so even combined the statements leave two answers.

questions.prompt:
What was a car's average speed for a journey?

(1) The journey covered 210 km.
(2) It began at 08:15 and ended at 11:15.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance over time. (1) gives the distance but no duration, and (2) gives 3 hours but no distance. Together, 210 km in 3 hours is 70 km/h. Each statement supplies exactly one of the two things the calculation needs.

questions.prompt:
What is the price of one book?

(1) Five books cost less than GBP 60.
(2) Three books cost GBP 31.50.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) only says the price is under GBP 12, which fits GBP 9 and GBP 11 alike. (2) divides exactly: GBP 31.50 over three books is GBP 10.50 each. The two are consistent, since five books at GBP 10.50 come to GBP 52.50, comfortably under GBP 60.

questions.prompt:
What is the area of a circle?

(1) Its circumference is 12 times pi centimetres.
(2) Its diameter is 12 centimetres.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1), circumference is 2 pi r, so r is 6 and the area is 36 pi square centimetres. From (2), a diameter of 12 also gives r = 6 and the same area. The two statements say the same thing in different words, so each alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt:
Which theatre sells the most tickets in a year?

Theatre | Seats | Performances a year | Average occupancy | Ticket price
Alderwood | 420 | 180 | 66% | GBP 22.00
Birchgate | 900 | 120 | 61% | GBP 31.00
Coombe | 260 | 240 | 88% | GBP 17.00
Dunhaven | 1,200 | 95 | 55% | GBP 40.00
Elmcourt | 640 | 210 | 69% | GBP 26.00
Fairhaven | 350 | 150 | 81% | GBP 19.00
questions.explanation: Tickets sold are seats multiplied by performances multiplied by occupancy: Alderwood 49,896, Birchgate 65,880, Coombe 54,912, Dunhaven 62,700, Elmcourt 92,736, Fairhaven 42,525. Elmcourt is highest without leading on any single column: Dunhaven has the most seats and Coombe the best occupancy at 88%. Three middling figures multiplied together beat one outstanding one.

questions.prompt:
Which theatre takes the most in ticket revenue in a year?

Theatre | Seats | Performances a year | Average occupancy | Ticket price
Alderwood | 420 | 180 | 66% | GBP 22.00
Birchgate | 900 | 120 | 61% | GBP 31.00
Coombe | 260 | 240 | 88% | GBP 17.00
Dunhaven | 1,200 | 95 | 55% | GBP 40.00
Elmcourt | 640 | 210 | 69% | GBP 26.00
Fairhaven | 350 | 150 | 81% | GBP 19.00
questions.explanation: Revenue is tickets sold multiplied by the ticket price: Alderwood GBP 1,097,712.00, Birchgate GBP 2,042,280.00, Coombe GBP 933,504.00, Dunhaven GBP 2,508,000.00, Elmcourt GBP 2,411,136.00, Fairhaven GBP 807,975.00. Dunhaven takes the most, though Elmcourt sells more tickets — 92,736 against 62,700. The dearer seat more than makes up the difference in volume.

questions.prompt:
How many theatres sell more than 60,000 tickets a year?

Theatre | Seats | Performances a year | Average occupancy | Ticket price
Alderwood | 420 | 180 | 66% | GBP 22.00
Birchgate | 900 | 120 | 61% | GBP 31.00
Coombe | 260 | 240 | 88% | GBP 17.00
Dunhaven | 1,200 | 95 | 55% | GBP 40.00
Elmcourt | 640 | 210 | 69% | GBP 26.00
Fairhaven | 350 | 150 | 81% | GBP 19.00
questions.explanation: Tickets sold: Alderwood 49,896, Birchgate 65,880, Coombe 54,912, Dunhaven 62,700, Elmcourt 92,736, Fairhaven 42,525. Above 60,000: Birchgate, Dunhaven, Elmcourt — 3 theatres. Coombe comes nearest to the line from below at 54,912, and the six theatres sell 368,649 tickets between them.

questions.prompt:
How many theatres are above the median on occupancy and below the median on seats?

Theatre | Seats | Performances a year | Average occupancy | Ticket price
Alderwood | 420 | 180 | 66% | GBP 22.00
Birchgate | 900 | 120 | 61% | GBP 31.00
Coombe | 260 | 240 | 88% | GBP 17.00
Dunhaven | 1,200 | 95 | 55% | GBP 40.00
Elmcourt | 640 | 210 | 69% | GBP 26.00
Fairhaven | 350 | 150 | 81% | GBP 19.00
questions.explanation: The medians are 67.5% occupancy and 530 seats. Above on occupancy: Coombe, Elmcourt, Fairhaven. Below on seats: Alderwood, Coombe, Fairhaven. On both: Coombe, Fairhaven — 2. Small houses do tend to fill better here, but not every one of them does.
